findings_unaided: Account 4100, Service revenue: the table shows this fell $82,000 (down 7.5 percent) but S2 says it grew $82,000 on Southline contract renewals -- one of these has the direction backwards.
Account 4300, Supplier rebates: jumped $172,000, up 409.5 percent, and it is marked with an asterisk as over threshold, but I do not see a commentary line that actually explains the rebate increase.

Account 7300, Legal settlement accrual: a brand new $185,000 charge this month, but S9 says no new legal matters arose in August -- if the accrual is new this month that reads as a legal matter for August even if the underlying claim is older.

Account 6050, Temporary labor: up $86,800 to $121,400, a 250.9 percent jump, the biggest percentage move on the page -- the Northgate summer peak story sounds reasonable but the size of it made me want to flag it.
S6 fuel and freight note: three August invoices totaling $31,200 were posted to September instead of August -- wondering if that means August freight and fuel numbers are a bit light this month.

C1.reason: Agreed, the $172,000 rebate jump on 4300 has no driver anywhere in the memo, that gap is real.

C2.reason: I did not rerun the margin math myself, but if unrounded numbers move it off 22 percent then the S11 conclusion should not stand.

C3.reason: Right, the table shows 4100 falling $82,000 while S2 says it grew, the direction in the sentence is just wrong.

C4.reason: The table shows warehouse wages, account 6000, moved only $37,700, not $86,800, so this one does not match what I read.

C5.reason: Makes sense, if the $185,000 accrual on 7300 relates to a claim resolved back in June then August is the wrong period for it.

C6.reason: S4 says temporary labor rose $68,800 but the table for 6050 shows $86,800, so the sentence and the schedule do not agree.

C7.reason: Fair point, $1,700 on bad debt is under the threshold and S7 spends more words on it than the big unexplained lines get.

C8.reason: S9 says no new legal matters in August and S10 books a new $185,000 accrual the same month, those cannot both stand as written.

C9.reason: That tracks, freight billed only rose $5,400 against a $27,600 rise in inbound freight and nobody in the memo mentions the squeeze on margin.

C10.reason: Adding temporary labor at Northgate does not really explain inbound freight costs, that driver sounds like it belongs to the 6050 labor line instead.

C11.reason: Right, the $31,200 in S6 belongs to August by its own description, so posting it to September is a cutoff problem worth flagging.

C12.reason: Insurance is flat at $47,300 with zero movement and no asterisk, pulling a policy schedule for an unchanged line seems like effort spent on nothing.

C13.reason: Fair, S1 just asserts the restaurant channel drove the $507,000 gain and I have not actually seen anything backing that up.

C14.reason: Something is off on 7100 either way, the table says $12,300 moved and S8 quotes $16,100, so the sentence needs to be restated.
